title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 85
paragraphs: When the Aeginetans heard that Cleomenes was dead, they sent envoys to Sparta to denounce Leotychides for the business of the hostages being kept at Athens. The Lacedaemonians convened a court and judged that Leotychides had outrageously wronged the Aeginetans; they sentenced him to be handed over, taken to Aegina, and surrendered in place of the men still held at Athens. But just as the Aeginetans were about to take Leotychides away, Theasides son of Leoprepes, a man of standing in Sparta, spoke to them. “What are you planning to do, men of Aegina? To carry off the king of the Spartans, handed over to you by his own fellow citizens? The Spartans may have voted this in anger now, but be careful lest at some later date — if you do it — they bring down ruin on your country. ” Hearing this, the Aeginetans held back from taking him. Instead they came to an agreement: Leotychides would accompany them to Athens and have the men returned to Aegina.
